title: Roger Taylor (Queen drummer) - Wikipedia
notes: Roger Meddows Taylor, born 26 July 1949 at West Norfolk and Lynn Hospital, King's Lynn; moved to Truro, Cornwall, as a child. At seven a ukulele band, the Bubblingover Boys; guitar first, then the drums, for which he found a more natural aptitude; taught himself to tune them, inspired by Keith Moon's 'great drum sounds' on the early Who records. At 15 joined Johnny Quale and the Reactions. Dentistry at the London Hospital Medical College from 1967, then a BSc in biology at East London Polytechnic. Met Brian May and Tim Staffell in 1968 (Smile, about two years, nine songs); Queen with Freddie Mercury; turned down Genesis in 1970. Influences: Mitch Mitchell his early role model ('just fantastic'); John Bonham 'the greatest rock and roll drummer of all time'; Buddy Rich 'the best I've ever seen'; Keith Moon 'absolutely brilliant', a 'total unique style' (Modern Drummer, 1984). At least one song on every Queen album; wrote or co-wrote These Are the Days of Our Lives, Innuendo and Under Pressure (UK number ones), Radio Ga Ga, A Kind of Magic, Heaven for Everyone, Breakthru, The Invisible Man. The Cross (1987-93), on guitar and lead vocals. A countertenor range. Planet Rock listeners' eighth-greatest classic rock drummer (2005); Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with Queen, 2001; OBE, 2020.

title: Robert Santelli, 'Roger Taylor', Modern Drummer, October 1984 (transcribed at pcpki.com)
notes: 'The whole thing is down to the song. "What does the song need?" is the main question.' 'Heads should be bright and responsive, and for that, you need a thin head.' 'I hate hitting loose skins.' 'After every song, I retune my snare drum.' Keith Moon's advice: 'Just make the bottom skin a little tighter than the top skin.' 'I use Ludwig'; 'a single bass drum and a selection of toms from small to big'; 'Zildjian and a few Paistes', changed round each tour. 'I always liked John Bonham, although in England he wasn't that fashionable'; Moon 'absolutely brilliant' in the early days; 'Stewart Copeland sort of provided the value of small drums.' The snap 'comes from' the wrists. We Will Rock You: 'It's feet', on an old drum podium. He uses a LinnDrum and 'a Simmons kit sprinkled around my kit', and often begins writing on a Linn or a Simmons sequencer.

title: Fraser Lewry, 'Roger Taylor on the Trident drum sound', Louder, 24 January 2025
notes: Quoting Taylor in Queen The Greatest, episode 6 ('The Drum Sound'): Trident's drum booth was 'very dry and dead, which is not what I wanted ... I wanted to hear the drums resonate. I didn't want it to go "thud, whack".' 'There was cloth over everything, and everything was taped down.'

title: 'How to drum and sound like Queen's Roger Taylor', Mixdown
notes: A gear guide, secondary: Ludwig from Smile in the late 1960s, a 26x14 bass drum, a 12-inch rack tom and 16- and 20-inch floor toms, 15-inch Zildjian hats; for the first two Queen tours a 26x14 kick, 13-inch rack tom, 16- and 18-inch floor toms; a Ludwig Speed King pedal; later DW.

title: Corey Irwin, 'Taylor Hawkins' Classic Rock Influences: In His Own Words', Ultimate Classic Rock, 28 March 2022
notes: Hawkins in Rhythm, 2002: 'Roger gave Queen their heavy feel and big sound.' 'He swings like no one else, and that's impossible to emulate.'

title: A composite image supplied by the owner (2026-10-19): Taylor in the mid-1980s beside a drum kit of his
notes: Taylor: a tousled blond feathered mullet past the collar, clean-shaven, a purple button-down shirt open over a white T-shirt, a pale cream textured blazer. The kit: blue sparkle shells, chrome hardware, a lighter teal sparkle snare, clear bottom heads on the toms, a white bass drum head with a black-and-orange graphic of a face, Istanbul Agop and Paiste cymbals and a large Paiste gong. The kit, with modern microphones and Istanbul Agop cymbals, is a recent one, not the 1980s'. The image carries no credit or date.

title: Queen (Queen album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 13 July 1973 (UK, EMI); Trident and De Lane Lea; produced by John Anthony, Roy Thomas Baker and Queen. Keep Yourself Alive a single on 6 July 1973. Taylor credited as Roger Meddows-Taylor, drums, percussion, vocals.

title: Sheer Heart Attack - Wikipedia
notes: Released 8 November 1974; Trident, Rockfield, AIR and Wessex; produced by Roy Thomas Baker and Queen. Stone Cold Crazy credited to all four, from Mercury's Wreckage; fast and distorted, it presaged speed metal ('thrash metal before the term was invented', Q); covered by Metallica (1990), a Grammy.

title: A Night at the Opera (Queen album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 28 November 1975; seven studios (Trident, Olympic, Rockfield, Lansdowne, Sarm East, Roundhouse, Scorpio); produced by Roy Thomas Baker and Queen, engineered by Mike Stone. Taylor on timpani and gong on Bohemian Rhapsody, whose piano, bass and drum parts Mercury conceived and wrote down in blocks. I'm in Love with My Car his.

title: A Day at the Races (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 10 December 1976; The Manor, Sarm East and Wessex; produced by Queen, their first without Roy Thomas Baker. Somebody to Love, Mercury's gospel song, a single on 12 November 1976; Mercury, May and Taylor multi-tracked as a choir.

title: News of the World (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 28 October 1977; Sarm East and Wessex; produced by Queen with Mike Stone. Taylor on drums on every track but We Will Rock You (hand claps and stamping). We Are the Champions a single on 7 October 1977.

title: Jazz (Queen album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 10 November 1978; Mountain (Montreux) and Super Bear (Berre-les-Alpes); produced by Queen and Roy Thomas Baker. Fat Bottomed Girls (May) and Don't Stop Me Now (Mercury). Syndrum pads on Fun It.

title: The Game (Queen album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 30 June 1980; Musicland, Munich, June-July 1979 and February-May 1980; produced by Queen with Reinhold Mack. Crazy Little Thing Called Love, Mercury's tribute to Elvis Presley, a single on 12 October 1979; Another One Bites the Dust (Deacon) on 22 August 1980.

title: The Works (Queen album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 27 February 1984 (UK); Record Plant, Los Angeles, and Musicland, Munich; produced by Queen and Reinhold Mack. Taylor on 'acoustic and electronic drums', a drum machine on Radio Ga Ga (his). Hammer to Fall (May) played third at Live Aid.

title: Another One Bites the Dust - Wikipedia
notes: Deacon played almost every instrument; 'Roger Taylor added a drum loop'; produced by Reinhold Mack at Musicland. The bass line close to 110.
